summary: Iteration 2 backend testing complete. 20/20 pytest cases passed on the public preview URL covering: gallery upload (success + PNG round-trip via /api/files, non-image 400, oversize 8MB 400, unauth 401), member invite (create + duplicate 409), CSV bulk import (3 rows created), public guest RSVP (success + duplicate email 409 + capacity full 409 + rsvp-count), member one-click RSVP (success, duplicate 409, cancel, cancel-again 404, /me/rsvps enrichment, unauth 401), admin RSVP list (returns rsvps + total_seats, forbidden for members 403), Google OAuth callback (invalid session_id 401, missing body 422), regressions (admin/stats includes rsvps key, admin2 login, public gallery). Verified rsvps collection has indexes: id_1, event_id_1_email_1, event_id_1_user_id_1. All test-created members/events/gallery items cleaned up via module-scope fixture.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1025 lines — approaching the 700-line split threshold. Consider splitting into routers (auth, members, events/sessions/gallery, rsvps, storage) as features grow.

put_object/get_object are sync `requests` calls inside async endpoints (gallery_upload, serve_file) — blocks the event loop. Wrap in asyncio.to_thread or switch to httpx.AsyncClient for the object-storage calls.
MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES is enforced only after full read into memory; a hostile client can still send >8MB and consume RAM before rejection. Consider a streaming check with Content-Length pre-validation.

public_rsvp uses email as uniqueness key but does not enforce capacity check atomically — race between _check_capacity and insert_one could allow over-booking under concurrent load. Consider a transaction or optimistic recount.
/api/files/{path:path} is fully public but only checks gallery.is_deleted; if another module later stores files with the same path scheme they leak. Acceptable now but worth documenting.
